text:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: GPU OOM detected on gpu-node-17 (pod=realtime-serving-3). Alloc failed in runtime allocate_kv_cache. headroom_report shows ~1.2Gi free but container crashed. tagging oncall. thread opened 2761234567
samir: I'm on it. grabbing logs from the node. any affecting customers?
julia: I see container restart loop in k8s events, CrashLoopBackOff. nvml logs show OOM during allocation at ~2026-03-14T09:12:22Z.
max: paste of nvidia-smi output from node 17:
```
GPU 0: 24576 MiB total, 23100 MiB used
Processes: 1 python (PID 4221) using 22000 MiB
```
priya: but headroom_report from scheduler claimed 1.2Gi free — that was measured earlier before prefetch. suspect reserved blocks / prefetch pinned memory, or fragmentation.
samir: pulling allocator debug from runtime: attaching dmesg and runtime allocator trace.
infra-bot: attached logs: /var/log/redwood/runtime/gpu-alloc.log.gz (see last 200 lines)
julia: interesting: runtime reports 'reserve_block_claimed' entries right before OOM, then 'ghost_reserve' cleanup failed. sequence looks like: reserve_claim(8Mi), reserve_pin(8Mi), prefetch_kv_cache(6Mi), then alloc(1Gi) fails.
max: that pattern smells like small pinned reservations for KV prefetch eating into contiguous region, fragmentation prevents large allocation even though aggregate free memory is sufficient.
priya: exact error from process: "CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1024.00 MiB (GPU 0; 24.00 GiB total; 22.62 GiB already allocated; 1.18 GiB free; 8.00 MiB reserved)" — note reserved shows 8Mi.
samir: so allocator reports reserved=8Mi but actual usable free is less because of fragmentation and reserved pinned blocks spread across the heap.
julia: can we evict KV cache or force compact? any quick mitigations to recover without restart?
max: two immediate actions: 1) force-kill KV prefetch on that pod (should free pinned) 2) trigger runtime compaction which frees fragmented reserved blocks (we have a /admin/compact endpoint).
priya: customer impact: realtime-serving-3 is handling low-QPS for customer 'atlas' — several requests returned 503s for ~2 minutes, logs show token-level failures. need to update status page.
samir: executing: `kubectl exec -n serving realtime-serving-3 -- pkill -f kv_prefetch`
ops-bot: command run by samir at 2761234678: returned 0
julia: after pkill, we see drop in pinned reservations in allocator logs and a few small allocations freed but still fragmentation remains. attempting compaction now: `curl -X POST http://gpu-node-17:8080/admin/compact`
infra-bot: compact endpoint acked, job queued.
max: compaction completed in ~12s. allocator trace shows coalesced free regions, then the pending allocation succeeded and process recovered.
priya: pod restarted earlier; now it is running stable again. customer 'atlas' ticket: transient errors observed ~2m starting 09:12Z.
samir: pushing quick postmortem notes: root cause = interplay of KV prefetch pinned small reserves + allocator fragmentation -> large allocation request couldn't find contiguous block despite aggregated headroom. visibility issue: headroom_report shows aggregate free but doesn't account for scattered pinned/reserved regions.
julia: mitigation checklist: - add prefetch cap to avoid pinning >X small blocks concurrently - expose contiguous_free metric in headroom_report - add auto-compact trigger when alloc fails with fragmentation signature - fallback to smaller model/streaming response on OOM to reduce contiguous req size
max: immediate: add circuit-breaker to prefetch path (limit concurrent prefetch per worker) and enable auto-compact on 2 consecutive reserve-failures.
priya: I'll update status page and notify customer success to liaise with 'atlas'.
samir: handing off to night oncall @priya at 2761234801 — priya, please monitor GPU node-17 until 12h mark and confirm no recurrence.
priya: ack. I'll also disable aggressive prefetch for that deployment as a temporary config: `PREFETCH_MAX_BLOCKS=4`.
ops-bot: follow-up reminder set for 2761238400 to check recurrence and schedule deeper alloc telemetry audit.
julia: saving allocator traces to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/2761234567/alloc-trace.log.gz
samir: postmortem owner: julia. ETA initial writeup 24h.
priya: quick customer-facing blurb drafted: "We experienced a transient serving disruption due to GPU memory fragmentation caused by prefetch reservations; we've applied mitigations and are investigating long-term fixes."
infra-bot: incident closed in channel at 2761234899 (status: mitigated, severity: P2)
